name: Necros
label: Touch and Go
lede: Skate-park kids from a Toledo suburb made Touch and Go's first record, lent their drummer to the Misfits for their last show, and gave the label the bass player who would run it for thirty years.

eras.title: Skate park to basement
eras.text: Necros came out of Maumee, Ohio, a suburb of Toledo, though everyone filed them with Detroit. The members were skateboarders first; the band started as talk on the ride home and didn't rehearse for a year.

years.h: Necros starts in Todd Swalla's mom's car in Maumee, Ohio
years.p: Barry Henssler, Todd Swalla and Andy Wendler are skaters from Maumee. Swalla says the band was born on a drive home from the skate park, then practiced in his basement for a couple of years.
years.xp: Swalla's mother taught music in the Toledo public schools and encouraged the noise. Necros went through four bassists before Corey Rusk: David Cooke, Brian Hyland, Jeff Lake and Brian Pollack, who later switched to guitar.

eras.title: Touch and Go's first band
eras.text: A zine sent through the mail got Necros to Tesco Vee and Dave Stimson, who ran the Touch and Go fanzine in East Lansing and were turning it into a label. Necros made its first release, a split pressing with Dischord, and brought in Corey Rusk, who ended up owning the whole thing.

years.h: Barry Henssler mails his zine to Tesco Vee
years.p: Barry Henssler sends his zine, Smegma Journal, to [[Tesco Vee|b988565c-c8c3-4491-b9ec-131cdb0df9be]] and Dave Stimson of the Touch and Go fanzine. They become fans of Necros and decide to put out a record.

years.h: Sex Drive EP, Touch and Go's first record
years.p: Four songs, and the first release on Touch and Go. About 25 sleeves were printed in a Sex Pistols-style design before it was dropped; the rest were thrown out when Dave Stimson's parents redecorated.

years.h: Corey Rusk joins on bass and starts running Touch and Go
years.p: [[Corey Rusk|7e85d4b9-f01b-4d5f-892b-523daae2917c]] becomes Necros' bassist in 1981 and joins Tesco Vee in running Touch and Go the same year.

years.h: IQ32, produced by Ian MacKaye, out on Touch and Go and Dischord
years.p: Nine songs, produced by [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]]'s [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and released jointly by Touch and Go and Dischord. It went through three pressings of 1,000, on green, tan and white labels.
years.xp: Dischord numbered it 4 1/2. A special run of 100 came in hand-numbered sleeves for a show at the Endless Summer skatepark.

years.h: Conquest for Death, Necros' first LP · Touch and Go
years.p: Necros' album for Touch and Go, with a 7-inch of the same name. [[Pushead|404f318c-a6c4-43ed-892a-a431d0ad4b2b]] drew the artwork for the single.

years.src: Wikipedia: Touch and Go Records · The Punk Vault
years.h: Corey Rusk leaves Necros to run Touch and Go
years.p: When Tesco Vee leaves Michigan in 1983, he hands Touch and Go to Corey Rusk and his wife Lisa. Rusk quits Necros for the label, and Ron Sakowski takes over on bass.
years.xp: The Punk Vault says Rusk and Barry Henssler would end up hating each other. The Rusks later moved Touch and Go to Chicago.

years.h: Todd Swalla drums for the Misfits at their last show
years.p: Necros open for the [[Misfits|936addc3-91aa-49de-8ec0-0dc186de151f]] at Graystone Hall in Detroit. The Misfits' drummer can't play, so Necros' Todd Swalla sits in: the last show of the original Misfits.
years.xp: Swalla told No Echo it was his second time filling in for the Misfits: he had rehearsed twice with them for an Irving Plaza show in New York. The Detroit one was spontaneous.

eras.title: Going metal, going under
eras.text: Without Rusk, Necros got heavier and slower, and Henssler kept it going with bigger ambitions. They opened for Black Flag, Bad Brains, Minor Threat and Sonic Youth, then went out with metal bands on a manager's bookings, chasing a major-label deal that didn't come.

years.h: Jail Jello with White Flag, and the Tangled Up 7-inch
years.p: Necros splits a 12-inch, Jail Jello, with [[White Flag|ad82f8fd-206f-4b62-9a0d-f46557edb725]] and releases the Tangled Up 7-inch, both on Gasatanka.

years.h: On tour with Megadeth, Overkill and Motörhead
years.p: Necros tours with [[Megadeth|a9044915-8be3-4c7e-b11f-9e2d2ea0a91e]] and [[Overkill|97fa7dd1-4706-4fad-b6ff-e099a37837fc]], and plays with [[Motörhead|57961a97-3796-4bf7-9f02-a985a8979ae9]] and [[Die Kreuzen|7550b236-f9c2-450c-81a6-fac63bf9d23e]] at the Olympic Auditorium. Todd Swalla says Megadeth drummer Chuck Behler later wore a Necros shirt on an album.
Necros' metal-leaning second album comes out on Restless.

q: It just felt like it was time to pack it in.
years.h: Elektra passes, and Necros calls it quits
years.p: After touring most of 1986, Necros is turned down by Elektra and breaks up in 1987.

eras.title: Laughing Hyenas and Negative Approach
eras.text: The members turned up across the Detroit scene's next chapters, and the label their old bassist ran became one of the biggest independents in America before scaling back in 2009.

years.p: A Necros live album comes out three years after the breakup. Rykodisc later paired it with Tangled Up on the band's only CD, in 2005.

years.h: Big Chief on Sub Pop; Laughing Hyenas on Touch and Go
years.p: Barry Henssler forms [[Big Chief|9e590e39-4fd6-4189-bfec-b698056a6999]], who record for Sub Pop. Todd Swalla and Ron Sakowski reunite in [[Laughing Hyenas|a3e6d60a-34ff-4d99-8397-2db6b5b2333e]] on Touch and Go, fronted by [[John Brannon|a3418f6c-a8b1-4565-9836-b389b405510a]] of [[Negative Approach|286e4fb9-4d6a-40de-ac50-01eff6a3c13e]].

years.h: Ron Sakowski joins the reunited Negative Approach
years.p: Ron Sakowski becomes bassist in [[Negative Approach|286e4fb9-4d6a-40de-ac50-01eff6a3c13e]] when the Detroit band reunites in 2006.

years.h: Corey Rusk scales Touch and Go back
years.p: Former Necros bassist Corey Rusk announces Touch and Go will shut down its manufacturing and distribution services, citing the economy.

years.h: SorceN: three Necros with a new singer
years.p: Todd Swalla, Andy Wendler and Ron Sakowski play two shows as SorceN, with Eric Oblander singing.

sources.title: setlist.fm: Misfits at Graystone Hall, October 29, 1983
